name: L3
notes: INSPIRE's own long_name for this record is simply 'L3 Experiment' (src:l3-inspire-experiment-record); no fetched source gives an expansion of 'L3' as an acronym, consistent with it denoting 'the third LEP experiment' proposal rather than an acronym.

The L3+C cosmic-ray extension (recognised as a CERN experiment from April 1998, using L3's magnet and muon chambers) is mentioned by CERN Courier but is out of scope here as a separate, un-owned experiment id.

physics_goals.locator: 'The Construction of the L3 Experiment', Nucl.Instrum.Meth.A 289 (1990) 35, abstract
physics_goals.quote: It is the only detector that concentrates its efforts on limited goals of measuring electrons, muons and photons. By not attempting to identify hadrons, L3 has been able to provide an order of magnitude better resolution for electrons, muons and photons.
physics_goals.value: Measure electrons, muons and photons with an order-of-magnitude better resolution than general-purpose detectors, by not attempting hadron identification

summary.plain: One of four giant detectors on CERN's LEP electron-positron collider from 1989 to 2000, built to measure electrons, muons and photons with exceptional precision using bismuth-germanate crystals and a huge magnet.
summary.technical: General-purpose LEP detector at interaction Point 2, optimised (rather than generalised) for electron, muon and photon measurements: a silicon-strip microvertex detector and time-expansion chamber for tracking, a BGO electromagnetic calorimeter, a hadron calorimeter and a muon spectrometer inside a very large solenoid. Approved by the CERN LEPC on 18 November 1982; ran from August 1989 to November 2000. Its magnet was reused as ALICE's solenoid at the same point after LEP shut down.

unique_capabilities.quote: electromagnetic calorimeter (called the 'BGO' - it was made of bismuth germanium oxide)
unique_capabilities.value: A bismuth-germanate (BGO) electromagnetic calorimeter for very high resolution photon and electron measurements
